title: What is the perimeter of a regular triangle, pentagon and hexagon?
description: A figure with all sides equal has a perimeter that is the number of sides times the side length. The video writes the rule for a triangle, a pentagon and a hexagon with a letter for the side, and checks it with a side of two centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal sides mean the side is added again and again, so the perimeter is the number of sides times the side. Watch for students who add the number of sides to the side length.

video_script.why: A learner uses the perimeter rule of the square for other figures with equal sides, by taking the side as many times as there are sides.
video_script.substitution: The method of the square's perimeter, four times the side, used for three sides, five sides and six sides.
video_script.anchor: figures with all sides equal to a letter-number eigh
video_script.payoff_line: The perimeter of the triangle is three eigh

final_answer.spoken: the triangle has perimeter three eigh, the pentagon five eigh, and the hexagon six eigh

never_show: the products 3a, 5a, 6a before the answer beat
maths_rules: Let each side have length a.
A triangle has 3 equal sides, so the perimeter is a + a + a = 3 × a = 3a.
A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides, so the perimeter is 5 × a = 5a.
A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides, so the perimeter is 6 × a = 6a.
video_script.design: One idea: number of sides times the side. Assumes the square's perimeter rule. The three figures stay on the stage with their sides coloured. Wrong idea (not raised): adding the number of sides to the side.
